import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every sign-up on the control plane (`:8080`) creates a **workspace** (a tenant) and an **owner** user. Production starts with sign-up **closed**, because open sign-up lets anyone create tenants with their own budget and microVM quota. You open it on purpose, behind a captcha, rate limits and verified email. This guide covers the sign-up modes, the verify and reset flows, and the owner-only data export and workspace deletion. The dashboard pages are thin clients over the endpoints below.

## Sign-up modes

`PAL_SIGNUP_MODE` controls `POST /auth/signup`. Unset, it is `closed` when `PAL_ENV` is `prod`, `production` or `staging`, and `open` otherwise. Any other value stops the server at startup.

| Mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `closed` | Every sign-up gets `403 {"error":"sign-up is closed"}`. Default in prod. |
| `invite` | Needs an `inviteCode` bound to the email, else `403`. Requires `PAL_SIGNUP_INVITE_SECRET`. |
| `open` | Anyone, subject to the rate limit and captcha. Default in dev. |

## Sign up, verify, log in

<Steps>

1. `POST /auth/signup`

   Rate limit, then mode, then captcha. Creates a tenant and an owner user with `email_verified_at = NULL`, and mails a verification link.

2. Prod: `202 verificationRequired`

   No JWT is issued. Dev: 201 with a JWT straight away (verification is not enforced), and the mail goes to the server log.

3. Open the emailed link

   The dashboard page `/auth/verify?token=...` posts the token to `POST /auth/verify`. Single use, valid 24 hours.

4. `POST /auth/login`

   Returns the JWT. In prod, an unverified user gets 403 with code `email_unverified`, after the password has matched.

</Steps>

Against a dev stack (`make run-api`), sign-up is open and returns a token immediately. The log mailer prints the verification mail to the control-plane log.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/signup \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"new.user@example.com","password":"correct-horse-battery","name":"New User"}'
# 201 {"token":"...","user":{"id":"...","tenantId":"...","email":"new.user@example.com","name":"New User","role":"owner"}}

# grab the link from the log, then redeem the token from its ?token= value
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/verify \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"token":"<token from the link>"}'
# 200 {"verified":true}
```

## Email verification

- **Enforced in prod only.** Dev keeps one-step sign-up so `make dev` works unchanged, but still sends the mail so the flow is testable.
- The token is 32 random bytes, emailed as a link, valid **24 hours**, usable once. Only its SHA-256 is stored.
- Until verified (prod), sign-up returns no JWT and `POST /auth/login` returns `403 {"error":"email not verified","code":"email_unverified"}`. `POST /v1/runs` from an unverified user returns `403 {"code":"email_unverified"}` as a second check. API keys are not affected.
- Existing users and OAuth sign-ins count as verified. Google sign-in is verified too.
- Lost the link? `POST /auth/verify/resend` mails a fresh one to an unverified password user.
- A completed password reset also verifies the email.

## Password reset

`POST /auth/forgot` mails a link to `/auth/reset?token=...` on the dashboard. The token is valid **1 hour** and works once. A successful reset sets the new password, verifies the email, and burns every other outstanding reset link for that user. Passwords must be at least 12 characters. Reset applies to password (`local`) accounts only.

`/auth/forgot` and `/auth/verify/resend` return the same `202` body whether or not the address has an account, and the mail is sent in the background, so relay latency does not show in response time. In prod, signing up with an already-registered email returns the same `202 verificationRequired` as a new one. In dev it returns `409 email already registered`.

Links point at `OAUTH_DASHBOARD_URL` (default `http://localhost:3001`). Set it in any deployed environment or emailed links will point at localhost.

## Invite codes

Invite codes are stateless and email-bound: `<expiryUnix>.<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, lower(email) + "|" + expiryUnix)>`. There is no table and no admin API. A code works only for the email it was minted for and only until its expiry. Mint one on any machine that has the secret:

```bash
EXP=$(( $(date +%s) + 7*86400 )); EMAIL=new.user@example.com
echo "$EXP.$(printf '%s|%s' "$EMAIL" "$EXP" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$PAL_SIGNUP_INVITE_SECRET" -r | cut -d' ' -f1)"
```

The invitee sends it as `inviteCode` in the sign-up body. A missing, expired, malformed or wrong-email code gets `403 a valid invite code is required to sign up`.

## Captcha

Cloudflare Turnstile is verified server-side against `siteverify` with the caller IP. It is required when `PAL_TURNSTILE_SECRET` is set, and always required for `open` sign-up in prod. Closed deployments never call Turnstile. The client sends the widget token as `captchaToken`. The dashboard renders the widget when `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` is set at build time.

| Condition | Response |
| --- | --- |
| No token | `400 captcha is required` |
| Token rejected | `403 captcha verification failed` |
| Turnstile unreachable | `503 captcha verification unavailable` (fails closed) |
| Required but no secret configured | `503 sign-up is not available`. Startup refuses this in prod. |

## Rate limits

Counters are fixed-window and kept in Redis, keyed by client IP (and email where noted). The IP is the TCP peer. `X-Forwarded-For` is honored only when the peer is inside `PAL_TRUSTED_PROXIES`. Exceeding a limit returns `429`.

| Endpoint | Limit | Key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /auth/signup` | 10 / hour | IP |
| `POST /auth/login` | 10 / minute | IP, and separately email |
| `POST /auth/forgot`, `POST /auth/verify/resend` | 20 / hour, and 5 / hour | IP, and email (each endpoint has its own counters) |
| `POST /auth/verify`, `POST /auth/reset` | 20 / hour | IP (per endpoint) |

## Mailer

Verification and reset mail use the driver in `PAL_MAILER` (default `log`). Mail is plain text, sent in the background with a 30 s limit. A failed send is logged, not returned.

| Driver | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `log` | Delivers nothing. Dev logs recipient, subject and body (the link). Prod logs recipient and subject only, so tokens never reach prod logs. |
| `smtp` | Standard-library SMTP to `PAL_SMTP_ADDR`, upgraded with STARTTLS when offered. Credentials are refused over an unencrypted connection to a non-localhost server. |
| `http` | POSTs JSON `{from,to,subject,text}` to `PAL_MAIL_HTTP_URL` with `Authorization: Bearer PAL_MAIL_HTTP_TOKEN` (the shape of Resend's `/emails` API). 15 second timeout; a non-2xx response is an error. |

The From address is `PAL_MAIL_FROM` (default `PAL <no-reply@localhost>`). The remaining variables are in [Environment variables](/docs/reference/env-vars/).

## Export your data

`GET /v1/tenants/{id}/export` returns everything the workspace owns as one JSON document, sent with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="pal-export-<tenantId>.json"`. It needs an owner JWT, and the id must be your own tenant. Another tenant's id is `404` (existence is not leaked), a non-owner is `403 owner role required`, and no token is `401`.

```json
{
  "tenantId": "…",
  "exportedAt": "2026-10-27T12:00:00Z",
  "tables": {
    "agents": [ … ],
    "runs": [ … ],
    "tenants": [ { … } ]
  }
}
```

`tables` has one array per table that has a `tenant_id` column, discovered from the database catalog so new tables are included automatically, plus the tenant row. Credential columns are left out by name: any column with a `secret`, `token`, `key`, `password`, `hash`, `enc`/`encrypted`, `ciphertext` or `credential(s)` segment (for example `password_hash`, `agent_triggers.secret_enc`, `data_planes.reg_token_hash`), plus `provider_config` and `connector_installs.config`. Dedup keys (`idempotency_key`, `idem_key`, `replay_key`) and `key_prefix` are exported. A new credential column is excluded by default. The document is built in memory, so very large workspaces produce a large response.

## Delete a workspace

`DELETE /v1/tenants/{id}` permanently erases the workspace (the GDPR right to erasure). In one transaction it deletes every tenant-scoped row (runs and their journal events first, then agents, every other tenant table, users) and finally the tenant itself. It cannot be undone.

- It needs an owner JWT; otherwise `403 owner role required`.
- `403 may only purge your own tenant` if the id is not yours.
- Any failure rolls the whole transaction back and returns `500 internal error`. Nothing is removed.
- Success is `200 {"tenant_id":"…","deleted":{"runs":12,"agents":3,…}}`, a per-table row count.

The API has no confirmation parameter. The safeguard is in the dashboard: the **Your data** section on the **General** tab of **Settings** (owners only) has **Export data (JSON)** and **Delete workspace**. In the confirmation dialog, **Delete forever** stays disabled until you type `delete my workspace`.

Both tenant routes also carry the `admin` scope annotation. Scope enforcement is on by default when `PAL_ENV` is `prod`, `production` or `staging`, and off in dev. Set `PAL_AUTHZ_ENFORCE=0` to opt out (logged as a warning) or `=1` to force it on in dev. Row-level security is on in production whenever `PAL_APP_DB_PASSWORD` is set; without it the control plane refuses to start unless you set `PAL_RLS_ENFORCE=0`. Either way API keys are not owners, so they get `403`.

## Free-tier caps

Every new workspace, from password sign-up or a first Google login, starts with a hard-fail daily spend cap and a sandbox quota, so a new account cannot run up cost. The cap is the tenant-wide budget (the row `PUT /v1/budgets/tenant` edits; see [Budgets](/docs/build/budgets/)). The quota is the one `PUT /v1/runtime/quota` edits. An owner can raise or remove either. Existing workspaces and the seeded dev workspace are never touched. Set a variable to `off` or `0` to skip that cap.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAL_FREE_TIER_COST_USD_PER_DAY` | `2.00` | Tenant-wide LLM spend per day (hard fail, HTTP 402). |
| `PAL_FREE_TIER_MAX_VMS` | `2` | Concurrent sandbox VMs. Compute hours (4/day) and egress (1 GB/day) are fixed. |
| `PAL_FREE_TIER_RUNTIME_COST_USD_PER_DAY` | `1.00` | Sandbox spend per day. |

## Startup checks

The control plane refuses to start when:

- `PAL_SIGNUP_MODE` is not `open`, `invite` or `closed`.
- `invite` mode is set without `PAL_SIGNUP_INVITE_SECRET`.
- `PAL_MAILER` is unknown, or `smtp`/`http` lacks its address or URL.
- In prod, `open` mode has no `PAL_TURNSTILE_SECRET`.
- In prod, the mode is `open` or `invite` with `PAL_MAILER=log`, because new users could never receive their verification link.

## Endpoint reference

All `/auth/*` routes take JSON and need no Bearer token.

| Endpoint | Request | Success | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /auth/signup` | `{email, password (12+ chars), name, inviteCode, captchaToken}` | Dev `201 {token, user:{id, tenantId, email, name, role}}` (`name` defaults to the part of the email before `@`). Prod `202 {"verificationRequired":true,"message":"Check your email for a link to verify your account."}`, no JWT. | `400` invalid body, missing or invalid email, short password, `captcha is required`. `403` closed, bad invite, captcha failed. `409` dev only, `email already registered`. `429`. `503` captcha unavailable, `sign-up is not available`. |
| `POST /auth/login` | `{email, password}` | JWT and user as above | `401 invalid credentials`, `429`, prod `403` `email_unverified` |
| `POST /auth/verify` | `{token}` | `200 {"verified":true}` | `400 invalid or expired token` (unknown, reused, expired or wrong-purpose), `429` past 20 per hour per IP |
| `POST /auth/verify/resend` | `{email}` | `202 {"status":"ok","message":"If that address has an account, we've sent it a link."}` for any well-formed email | `400 a valid email is required`, `429` |
| `POST /auth/forgot` | `{email}` | Same responses and limits as resend; sends a reset link | |
| `POST /auth/reset` | `{token, password}` | `200 {"reset":true}` | `400` short password or `invalid or expired token`, `429`. The token is checked after the length, so a short password does not burn it. |

`GET /v1/tenants/{id}/export` and `DELETE /v1/tenants/{id}` take a Bearer owner JWT; see above.

## Teams

A workspace is one tenant. Sign-up creates its owner, and only the owner can export or delete it. The control plane has no member or invite API. The Settings page has a Team tab, but it keeps its member list in the browser's local storage, so it does not give anyone else access to the workspace. For shared programmatic access, [API keys](/docs/reference/api/) carry scopes; a key cannot be an owner.

## Limits

- Invite codes cannot be listed or revoked. To cancel one, rotate `PAL_SIGNUP_INVITE_SECRET`, which invalidates all of them.
- Rate limiting needs Redis. If Redis is absent or errors, the limiter fails open so an outage cannot lock owners out, and only the captcha and sign-up mode protect `/auth/*`.
- Emailed links use `OAUTH_DASHBOARD_URL`, which defaults to localhost.
